newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: AGRICULTURAL DECIDED ON SHARE CAPITAL BOOST.
newsitem.headline: AGRICULTURAL DECIDED ON SHARE CAPITAL BOOST.

text.p: Lithuania's state run Agricultural Bank said on Friday that its general shareholders' meeting decided to boost the bank's share capital by 42.875 million litas to 171 million litas by issuing new shares.
"The shareholders' of the bank decided to issue 245,000 ordinary shares with a face value of 175 litas," the head of the bank's treasury department, Valdas Bernatvichius, told Reuters.
He also said the move was necessary to meet the minimum 10 percent capital adequacy ratio required by the Bank of Lithuania. The banks' capital adequacy ratio stood at 9.18 percent as of May 1.
"The share capital boost will allow the bank to carry out a more agressive marketing policy and to increase the assets of the bank," Bernatavichius said.
Agricultural Bank is the second biggest bank in terms of assets which stood at 1.277 billion litas at the end of April.
Shareholders have one month to take up their priority rights to the new shares.
"The remaining shares will be distributed by an open subscription," Bernatavichius said.
"The council of the bank is expected to decide on the share issue price in the course of one month," he added.

Agricultural bank is one of the two state run banks which was slated for privatisation. The government said earlier it expected to chosse a privatisation advisor this year and to start the actual privatisation of the bank in 1998.
The bank posted a net profit of 25.5 million litas in 1996 and 11.24 million litas for the first quarter of the year.
The bank said on Friday its preliminary net profit for the five months of the year was down to 8.6 million litas.
